summary: SNK's long-running team-fighting series, covering the annual Neo Geo run, later numbered sequels, remakes, handheld/mobile spin-offs, Maximum Impact 3D entries, and major collections.

entries.title: The King of Fighters '94

emulation.notes: Upscale the PS2 remake; MAME/FinalBurn Neo is the fallback for the original arcade release.

primary.why: Re-Bout is the most complete official version of the first game, adding higher-resolution presentation, team edit, online play, playable Rugal, and Saisyu Kusanagi.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 Re-Bout release through PCSX2 at high internal resolution; use the original Neo Geo version only for historical arcade comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: Use the original Neo Geo version for pure arcade preservation; use Re-Bout for Sami's highest-fidelity/most-complete route.

entries.title: The King of Fighters '95
entries.definitive_edition: Sega Saturn release plus Game Boy secondary

emulation.emulator: Mednafen or Kronos; SameBoy for Game Boy secondary
emulation.notes: Use Saturn emulation for the main run and Game Boy emulation for the exclusive character route.

primary.why: The Saturn port is the strongest home route among the original-era releases, while the Game Boy version is a separate reduced adaptation with its own exclusive character.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Saturn version with a modern Saturn emulator; play the Game Boy adaptation only for its exclusive Nakoruru content.

secondary.exclusive_content: Nakoruru from Samurai Shodown is exclusive to the Game Boy adaptation.
secondary.what_to_play: Sample the Game Boy version for Nakoruru and its portable conversion differences.

entries.remaster_caveats: Orochi collection access is useful, but the handheld exclusive is still separate.

entries.title: The King of Fighters '96
entries.definitive_edition: Sega Saturn release plus Game Boy secondary

emulation.emulator: Mednafen or Kronos; SameBoy for Game Boy secondary
emulation.notes: Use Saturn emulation for the main run and Game Boy emulation for Mr. Karate.

primary.why: The Saturn port is documented as cartridge-assisted and includes code access to Chizuru and Goenitz, making it the strongest complete home route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Saturn version with a modern Saturn emulator; use the Game Boy Heat of Battle adaptation only for its exclusive Mr. Karate content.

secondary.exclusive_content: Mr. Karate is exclusive to the Game Boy adaptation.
secondary.what_to_play: Play the portable adaptation far enough to use/sample Mr. Karate.

entries.remaster_caveats: Anthology versions are useful for access, but do not replace the handheld exclusive content.

entries.title: The King of Fighters '97
entries.definitive_edition: The King of Fighters '97 Global Match

emulation.emulator: None for PC; Mednafen/Kronos for secondary ports
emulation.notes: Use the PC version for main play.

primary.version: The King of Fighters '97 Global Match
primary.why: Global Match is the practical modern version of the Orochi finale and adds online play while preserving the original game route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PC Global Match release; use Saturn/PlayStation only for original-console feature comparison.

secondary.exclusive_content: Saturn/PlayStation home features such as art-gallery material and code-based Orochi access.
secondary.what_to_play: Sample the home-console extras if archival completeness matters.
secondary.why: The Saturn and PlayStation ports include special home-console features.

entries.remaster_caveats: Keep Saturn/PlayStation noted for archival extras.

entries.title: The King of Fighters '98
entries.definitive_edition: The King of Fighters '98 Ultimate Match Final Edition

emulation.emulator: None for PC; Flycast for Dreamcast secondary
emulation.notes: Use native PC for the main run.

primary.version: The King of Fighters '98 Ultimate Match Final Edition
primary.why: Ultimate Match expands the roster and features, and Final Edition is the modern PC release tracked as a PC version.
primary.how_to_play: Play Ultimate Match Final Edition on PC; optionally sample Dream Match 1999 for its Dreamcast-specific 3D backgrounds and link features.

secondary.exclusive_content: Dreamcast-specific 3D backgrounds, extended animated introduction, and link-up feature with KOF R-2.
secondary.what_to_play: Sample Dream Match 1999 for its presentation and link-related content.

entries.remaster_caveats: Dream Match 1999 remains worth noting for Dreamcast-only presentation features.

entries.title: The King of Fighters '99

emulation.notes: Use Windows if available, otherwise emulate the Dreamcast Evolution version.

primary.why: Evolution is documented as the Dreamcast/Windows version with visual updates and extra striker/boss content, so the Windows release is the most practical complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows Evolution version where available; use Dreamcast emulation as the closest practical fallback.

entries.remaster_caveats: Availability of the Windows release can be awkward; Dreamcast emulation is the fallback.

entries.title: The King of Fighters 2000

primary.why: The Dreamcast release is the best original-generation home route for the second NESTS entry, with PS2 bundle access as a practical alternative.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Dreamcast release through Flycast at high output resolution; use the PS2 2000/2001 bundle only if collection convenience matters.

entries.remaster_caveats: PS2 bundle is a convenience package rather than a content-definitive upgrade.

entries.title: The King of Fighters 2001

primary.why: The Dreamcast release is the strongest standalone home route for KOF 2001, while the PS2 release is mainly a bundled/collection route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Dreamcast release through Flycast at high output resolution.

entries.remaster_caveats: Use PS2 only for collection convenience.

entries.title: The King of Fighters 2002
entries.definitive_edition: The King of Fighters 2002 Unlimited Match

primary.version: The King of Fighters 2002 Unlimited Match
primary.why: Unlimited Match is the expanded remake with a far larger roster and replacement/additional characters, and the PC version is the best modern route.
primary.how_to_play: Play The King of Fighters 2002 Unlimited Match on PC; play the Dreamcast/Xbox/PS2 versions only for historical comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: Original Dreamcast/PS2/Xbox versions are useful for historical comparison but are not the recommended main route.

entries.title: The King of Fighters 2003

emulation.notes: Prefer Xbox for output when stable; PS2 is the fallback.

primary.why: The Xbox/PS2 home releases are the practical final Neo Geo-era routes; Xbox emulation gives the highest output path for the home version.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox version through xemu if compatibility is acceptable; use the PS2 release through PCSX2 as fallback.

entries.remaster_caveats: The planned Dreamcast release was cancelled, so do not treat Dreamcast as a playable platform.

entries.title: The King of Fighters XI

primary.why: The PS2 version adds music, stages, and characters beyond the Atomiswave arcade release, making it the most complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 release through PCSX2 at high internal resolution.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern PC/console remaster is documented in the public series list.

entries.title: The King of Fighters XII

emulation.notes: Use whichever emulator is more stable for the user's library.

primary.why: KOF XII's HD home releases are PS3 and Xbox 360 after the Taito Type X2 arcade release; PS3 emulation is the most practical high-output route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS3 release through RPCS3 or the Xbox 360 version through Xenia if preferred.

entries.remaster_caveats: KOF XII is a lean, storyless entry with a small roster; KOF XIII is the stronger follow-up, but not the same game.

entries.title: The King of Fighters XIII
entries.definitive_edition: The King of Fighters XIII Global Match

primary.version: The King of Fighters XIII Global Match
primary.why: Global Match is the current rollback-enabled version and PC offers the highest-fidelity route, while the older Steam Edition/GOG release remains a prior Climax-based PC route.
primary.how_to_play: Play The King of Fighters XIII Global Match on PC with current patches; use Steam Edition/GOG only if Global Match issues block play.

entries.remaster_caveats: If Global Match PC issues matter, retain the older Steam/GOG Climax-based version as a fallback when owned.

entries.title: The King of Fighters XIV
entries.definitive_edition: The King of Fighters XIV Ultimate Edition / Steam Edition with DLC

primary.why: The PC Steam Edition is the highest-fidelity official route, and the Ultimate Edition package bundles the game with DLC content.
primary.how_to_play: Play KOF XIV Steam Edition on PC with all DLC or the Ultimate Edition package.

entries.remaster_caveats: Base PS4 release lacks the full DLC package unless upgraded.

entries.title: The King of Fighters XV

primary.why: The PC release has the highest display flexibility for the latest mainline KOF and official platform support includes Windows/Steam/Epic alongside consoles.
primary.how_to_play: Play on PC with current patches and DLC installed.

entries.remaster_caveats: Choose PC for fidelity; console versions are valid if local setup/online community dictates.

entries.title: King of Fighters R-1

emulation.notes: Use accurate Neo Geo Pocket emulation.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original handheld fidelity with clean scaling

primary.why: R-1 is a Neo Geo Pocket adaptation of KOF '97, and the original handheld release is the defining version.
primary.how_to_play: Play via a Neo Geo Pocket emulator with LCD scaling/shader preferences.

entries.remaster_caveats: Not a replacement for KOF '97; treat it as its own handheld adaptation.

entries.title: King of Fighters R-2

emulation.notes: Use accurate Neo Geo Pocket Color emulation.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original handheld color fidelity with clean scaling

primary.platform: Neo Geo Pocket Color via emulator
primary.why: R-2 is the Neo Geo Pocket Color adaptation of KOF '98 and is documented as linkable with Dream Match 1999.
primary.how_to_play: Play via a Neo Geo Pocket Color emulator; use Dreamcast Dream Match 1999 separately if exploring the link feature.

entries.remaster_caveats: Not a replacement for KOF '98; it is a separate portable adaptation.

entries.title: The King of Fighters EX: Neo Blood

primary.why: EX: Neo Blood is a GBA-only adaptation of KOF '99 with a new story and new character Moe Habana.
primary.how_to_play: Play the GBA release via mGBA with integer scaling.

entries.remaster_caveats: Separate story adaptation, not a replacement for KOF '99.

entries.title: The King of Fighters EX2: Howling Blood

emulation.notes: Use GBA emulation for the primary route.

primary.why: EX2 is the GBA-native sequel/adaptation with its own story, new characters, and stage content; it is the cleanest route versus the retitled N-Gage port.
primary.how_to_play: Play the GBA version via mGBA; sample the N-Gage port only for curiosity.

entries.remaster_caveats: N-Gage version is retitled The King of Fighters: Extreme.

entries.title: The King of Fighters: Neowave

primary.why: Neowave is an Atomiswave remix of KOF 2002 with new presentation; the Xbox/PS2 home releases are the practical routes, with Xbox preferred for fidelity.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox version through xemu; use PS2 through PCSX2 if compatibility is better.

entries.remaster_caveats: Treat as a distinct KOF 2002 remix, not a replacement for 2002 Unlimited Match.

entries.title: KOF: Maximum Impact

primary.why: The Xbox/Maniax route adds dual-language audio and online-era features compared with the original PS2 release, making it the most complete version.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox Maniax version through xemu; use the PS2 version only if compatibility demands it.

entries.remaster_caveats: 3D spin-off continuity; do not conflate with mainline 2D KOF.

entries.title: KOF: Maximum Impact 2
entries.definitive_edition: The King of Fighters 2006 / Maximum Impact 2

primary.version: The King of Fighters 2006 / Maximum Impact 2
primary.why: Maximum Impact 2 is primarily a PS2-era 3D spin-off; the PS2 version is the practical complete route and the North American title is The King of Fighters 2006.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 release through PCSX2 at high internal resolution.

entries.remaster_caveats: Distinct Maximum Impact continuity; not a mainline numbered entry.

entries.title: KOF Maximum Impact: Regulation A

primary.why: Regulation A remakes the Maximum Impact branch with new characters and classic 3-on-3 gameplay; the PS2 release is the practical home route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 release through PCSX2 at high internal resolution.

entries.remaster_caveats: The planned Regulation A2 sequel was cancelled, so it is not included as a playable entry.

entries.title: The King of Fighters '95 (Game Boy)

emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Game Boy original with clean scaling

primary.why: This is the distinct Game Boy adaptation of KOF '95 and includes Nakoruru, so it deserves its own handheld route.
primary.how_to_play: Play with SameBoy or another accurate Game Boy emulator.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not treat this as the definitive KOF '95 main game; it is the portable adaptation.

entries.title: The King of Fighters: Heat of Battle

emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Game Boy original with clean scaling

primary.why: Heat of Battle is the localized Game Boy adaptation of KOF '96 and includes handheld-specific content such as Mr. Karate.
primary.how_to_play: Play with SameBoy or another accurate Game Boy emulator.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not treat this as the definitive KOF '96 main game; it is the portable adaptation.

entries.title: The King of Fighters '94 Re-Bout

primary.why: Re-Bout is the enhanced KOF '94 remake with higher-resolution presentation and added playable content.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 version through PCSX2 at high internal resolution.

entries.remaster_caveats: Use original Neo Geo KOF '94 separately for arcade-authentic preservation.

entries.title: The King of Fighters '97 Global Match
entries.definitive_edition: The King of Fighters '97 Global Match

primary.why: Global Match is the modern release of KOF '97 and PC is the most flexible route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PC version with current patches.

entries.remaster_caveats: Older Saturn/PlayStation home extras remain documented under the base KOF '97 entry.

entries.title: The King of Fighters '98 Ultimate Match Final Edition
entries.definitive_edition: The King of Fighters '98 Ultimate Match Final Edition

primary.why: Final Edition is the modern PC version of the expanded KOF '98 Ultimate Match, making it the best current route for this remake.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PC Final Edition with current patches.

entries.remaster_caveats: Dreamcast Dream Match 1999 remains a separate presentation variant, covered under the base KOF '98 entry.

entries.title: The King of Fighters 2002 Unlimited Match
entries.definitive_edition: The King of Fighters 2002 Unlimited Match

primary.why: Unlimited Match expands KOF 2002 with a replacement character and a much larger roster, and PC is the highest-fidelity current route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PC release with current patches.

entries.remaster_caveats: Treat original 2002 separately for tournament/historical preservation if needed.

entries.title: The King of Fighters XIII Global Match
entries.definitive_edition: The King of Fighters XIII Global Match

primary.why: Global Match adds rollback-era online functionality to KOF XIII, and the PC release gives the highest-fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PC Global Match release with current patches.

entries.remaster_caveats: Global Match became a separate PC purchase after the older Steam Edition route.

entries.title: The King of Fighters 2000/2001

primary.why: This compilation bundles KOF 2000 and 2001 on PS2 and is useful as a collection route rather than a replacement for the individual Dreamcast picks.
primary.how_to_play: Play through PCSX2 if you want the double-pack presentation.

entries.remaster_caveats: Use individual entries for best-version picks of each included game.

entries.title: The King of Fighters 2002/2003

primary.why: This compilation bundles KOF 2002 and 2003 on Xbox/PS2; Xbox is preferred for the highest home-console output route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox version through xemu, or PS2 through PCSX2 if compatibility is better.

entries.remaster_caveats: Use individual entries for best-version picks of each included game.

entries.title: The King of Fighters Collection: The Orochi Saga

primary.why: The collection packages the Orochi-era games and adds challenge/media-gallery content; PS2 emulation offers the highest-fidelity route among the listed platforms.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 version through PCSX2 for anthology access; use individual entries for exact best-version recommendations.

entries.remaster_caveats: The collection is convenient, but individual game entries still carry the true best-version picks and secondaries.

entries.title: The King of Fighters: NESTS Collection

primary.why: The NESTS Collection packages KOF '99, 2000, and 2001 on PS2; PCSX2 gives the highest-fidelity route for this anthology.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 collection through PCSX2; use individual entries for exact best-version choices.

entries.remaster_caveats: Collection convenience does not override the individual Dreamcast/Windows picks for the included games.

entries.title: Quiz King of Fighters

emulation.emulator: MAME / FinalBurn Neo / Neo Geo CD emulator
emulation.notes: Use the Neo Geo CD route for home play.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Neo Geo original with clean scaling

primary.why: Quiz King of Fighters is a Japan-only KOF-themed quiz game with arcade, Neo Geo, and Neo Geo CD releases; Neo Geo CD emulation is the most convenient home route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Neo Geo CD version through a Neo Geo CD-capable emulator, with the arcade/Neo Geo versions as alternatives.

entries.remaster_caveats: Japanese quiz spin-off; language knowledge affects playability.

entries.title: The King of Fighters: Kyo

primary.why: KOF: Kyo is a Japan-only PlayStation RPG spin-off, and the original PS1 release is the only documented platform.
primary.how_to_play: Play through DuckStation with high internal resolution and texture filtering to taste.

entries.remaster_caveats: Japan-only RPG spin-off; translation needs may affect practical play.

entries.title: The King of Fighters: Battle de Paradise

emulation.notes: Use accurate Neo Geo Pocket Color emulation.

primary.platform: Neo Geo Pocket Color via emulator
primary.why: Battle de Paradise is a Neo Geo Pocket Color board-game spin-off and the original handheld release is the documented route.
primary.how_to_play: Play with an accurate Neo Geo Pocket Color emulator.

entries.remaster_caveats: Japan-only board-game spin-off.

entries.title: King of Fighters: Sky Stage

emulation.notes: Use original Xbox 360 hardware if emulation is not stable.

primary.why: Sky Stage is the KOF shooting-game spin-off and the Xbox Live Arcade release is the practical home version of the arcade game.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox Live Arcade version on original hardware or through Xenia if compatibility is acceptable.

entries.remaster_caveats: Digital availability may depend on legacy Xbox account/hardware access.

entries.title: The King of Fighters-i 2012

primary.why: KOF-i 2012 is the documented iOS mobile KOF release with expanded character and mode content.
primary.how_to_play: Play on a compatible iOS device/account if still available in the user's purchase history or current regional store.

entries.remaster_caveats: Mobile store availability can change; archive as a mobile-only spin-off.

entries.title: The King of Fighters-A 2012

primary.why: KOF-A 2012 is the Android mobile version with its own mobile distribution route and documented character/mode content.
primary.how_to_play: Play on a compatible Android device through the official store route where available.

entries.remaster_caveats: Mobile OS/store compatibility can change over time.

entries.title: The Rhythm of Fighters

emulation.notes: Mobile app availability is the blocker.

primary.why: The Rhythm of Fighters was an Android/iOS rhythm-action spin-off and its service ended in 2015.
primary.how_to_play: No normal current storefront route; preserve through owned-device/app-history access or documentation only.

entries.remaster_caveats: Service ended July 15, 2015; this is an archive record more than a current play recommendation.

entries.title: The King of Fighters All Star
entries.definitive_edition: Final live-service build, no current normal route

primary.why: All Star was a mobile/Windows action-RPG spin-off, but the service ended on October 30, 2024.
primary.how_to_play: No normal current live route; archive through documentation, owned remnants, or official/offline materials if they exist.

entries.remaster_caveats: Ended service on October 30, 2024; do not present as normally playable.

entries.title: The King of Fighters for Girls

primary.why: For Girls is an Android/iOS mobile spin-off released in 2019.
primary.how_to_play: Use the official mobile route if still available in the relevant region/account; otherwise treat as an archive-only mobile entry.

entries.remaster_caveats: Mobile availability is region/account dependent; archive carefully.
